reasoning.step1:
I will identify invoice indicators, verify document classification, locate each required field, consider alternatives, and decide whether values can be extracted without inference.

1) Document classification (invoice vs non-invoice)
- Look for invoice indicators: I see the word "Rechnung" (German for Invoice) clearly near the top. There is an invoice number line "Nummer: 2400124 Datum: 25.01.2024", totals, VAT lines, line items, and payment/IBAN details. No exclusion indicators such as "Zahlungserinnerung" or "Mahnung" or "Servicebericht" are present. Keyword density favors invoice indicators. Conclusion: this is an invoice — proceed with extraction.

2) Locate potential fields required by schema
Schema requires: GrandTotal.Amount, Invoice.Date, Sender.VatId, Vat.Rate (one or more), Net.Amount, Vat.Amount (corresponding to each Vat.Rate).

Scan the text for each:

- Invoice.Date:
  - Text shows "Nummer: 2400124 Datum: 25.01.2024". This gives a clear date string "25.01.2024". Candidate value: "25.01.2024".

- Sender.VatId:
  - Look for VAT/UID lines. Text contains "Unsere UID-Nr.: ATU 64424288". This is the sender VAT ID. Candidate value: "ATU 64424288". No other VAT IDs for sender are apparent.

- GrandTotal.Amount:
  - Look for total payable. Text: "Zahlung bis 08.02.2024 ohne Abzug Gesamtbetrag EUR 254,53". This indicates total amount payable EUR 254,53. Candidate numeric value: 254,53. Need to ensure decimal format preserved as in input; input uses comma as decimal separator. Schema expects a number type — but developer rules say keep decimals as in input and do not include currency symbol. We must represent numeric value; consider representation: maintain same decimal places (two) but convert comma to dot if required by JSON number. The schema allows number or empty. I'll note candidate numeric value 254.53 (converted) while remembering input was "254,53". Also check earlier lines: "Nettobetrag EUR 231,39" and "10% Mwst. von 231,39 EUR 23,14". So grand total 231,39 + 23,14 = 254,53 — consistent.

- Net.Amount:
  - "Nettobetrag EUR 231,39" clearly present. Candidate numeric: 231,39 (231.39).

- Vat.Amount:
  - "10% Mwst. von 231,39 EUR 23,14" shows VAT amount 23,14 (23.14). Candidate: 23,14.

- Vat.Rate:
  - The same line shows "10% Mwst." so VAT rate is 10%. Per rules, extract rate without percent symbol, so candidate rate: 10.

Consider possibility of multiple VAT groups:
- Invoice line items show "Mw% 10" in item table for each item. There is only one VAT rate (10%) used. So Vat.Item array will contain one entry with Rate=10, Net.Amount=231,39, Vat.Amount=23,14.

3) Verify No Inference rule and exactness
- All required values are explicitly present in invoice text: Invoice date, sender UID, net amount, VAT rate and VAT amount, total. No need to infer missing data.
- Maintain decimal places as in input (two decimals). For JSON numbers, decimals will use dot; but preserve numeric precision (two decimals).
- Sender.VatId should be string exactly as written "ATU 64424288".

4) Edge cases and alternatives
- The document contains two IBANs and other identifiers; ensure not to confuse those with VAT ID.
- There is also "Unsere UID-Nr.: ATU 64424288" — UID is VAT ID in Austria, so use that.
- Ensure GrandTotal corresponds to "Gesamtbetrag EUR 254,53". That is explicit.
- Ensure VAT.Amount corresponds to the VAT line "10% Mwst. von 231,39 EUR 23,14" — explicit.

5) Final mapping (values identified to place into JSON)
- Invoice.Date -> "25.01.2024"
- Sender.VatId -> "ATU 64424288"
- GrandTotal.Amount -> numeric 254.53 (input 254,53)
- Net.Amount -> numeric 231
